name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: French 10-year yield fell below 4.8% on 23 Nov, off October's 24-year high of 5.1%; no failed G7 auction found
state: The French 10-year yield fell below 4.8% on 23 Nov, helped by a safe-haven bid and President Macron's proposed constitutional budget rule, after peaking at a 24-year high of 5.1% in October; it is still about 125bp higher this year (Trading Economics). Weak November PMI data point to a possible French technical recession in the fourth quarter. No confirmed France–Bund spread above 150bp, failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank buying was found as of 25 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Governments, firms and households refinancing debt in France and other high-deficit G7 countries face higher borrowing costs than a year ago.
rubric_hit: Watch: G7 long yields near multi-decade highs (French 10y peaked 5.1% in Oct); no failed auction or >150bp spread

sources.title: Trading Economics — French Bond Yields Rise as ECB Rate Hike Bets Grow (with later updates)

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
